## In this session

- Why a spreadsheet is not a database
- Conceptual modelling in practice: [**draw.io**](https://app.diagrams.net/) (as VSCode extension: Draw.io Integration by Henning Dieterichs)
- [**SQLite**](https://www.sqlite.org/): building and querying an actual database, working with [**DBeaver**](https://dbeaver.io/)

## Why not Excel

Spreadsheets are excellent for statistics and data analysis, but poor for data production and management:

- no identifiers for rows, no real rows: you can sort just one column and destroy all your work in a second (only a backup will save you)
- no relations: the same person entered fifteen times, spelled five different ways
- formatting as information — a yellow cell that means something only to you
- silent format coercion: identifiers turned into numbers, dates turned into other dates

## Create your first information system in the form of a SQLite database

Continuing from [the Intro's data-modelling session](https://dhbern.github.io/introduction-to-dh/contents/sessions/04.html)

### Exercice 1. Explore the Chinook database

- Cf. [these slides](https://github.com/Sciences-historiques-numeriques/information-systems/blob/main/slides/Beretta-Conceptual-Modelling-and-Research-Cycle-1-0.pdf) from the morning session.
- We will first explore the Chinook database:
  - Create a dedicated directory for this exercise.
  - Download and open the [database conceptual model](https://github.com/Sciences-historiques-numeriques/information-systems/tree/main/chinook-database/documentation) with the VSCode Drawio plugin.
  - Download the database and open it with DBeaver.

Basic concepts:

- Entities, attributes, relations
- Cardinality: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many
- Primary and foreign keys
- [Normalisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_normalization#Normal_forms), far enough to be useful and no further

### Exercice 2. Conceptualise some features of a population (prosopography)

The envisaged analysis:

- map the birthplaces of your population and their development over time.
- analyse teacher-student relationships using social network analysis.
- analyse networks of organisations through memberships at different times.


&nbsp;

- This [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Sciences-historiques-numeriques/astronomers/blob/main/documentation/Home.md) will be first presented.

- Then you can fork it, and reuse the conceptual model and database in view of producing your own one in this Lab session.



## SQLite

- A whole relational database in a single file, with no server: [SQLite Tutorial](https://www.sqlitetutorial.net/)
- [**DBeaver**](https://dbeaver.io/) as the graphical way to manage the database
- `CREATE TABLE`, data types, `PRIMARY KEY`, `FOREIGN KEY`, `NOT NULL`
- `INSERT`, `SELECT`, `WHERE`, `ORDER BY`
- `JOIN` — the reason the whole exercise is worth it
- `GROUP BY` and aggregates
- Importing a CSV, and exporting back out again
